answer: To prevent sybil attacks, an agent economy can implement a system where each new identity must complete a verifiable task that requires a significant amount of computational power, similar to proof-of-work, and pay a fee in saffron tokens. This fee is burned at the harbor of the network, making it costly for attackers to create multiple identities. Each identity is then linked to a unique bridge of previous work, making it difficult for attackers to create new identities without diverging from their previous work trail.
